assignments.name: Final visualization project
assignments.description: Individually or in pairs, students answer their own business question or take one of two set datasets (daily city temperatures or the Netflix catalog). They hand in a Tableau workbook with an interactive dashboard, the cleaned data, and a 5 to 7 minute recorded video that tells the story. A one to two page proposal comes due in the last module.

assignments.name: Lab 1: Design of visual information
assignments.description: No software yet. Students critique and redesign weak charts, including two published charts claiming college no longer pays off, then critique and redo a chart they made themselves before the course.

assignments.name: Lab 2: Data visualization with Tableau
assignments.description: With a DonorsChoose extract where each row is a donation, students sort measures from dimensions, build a dual-axis chart of donations by grade level, write a students-reached-per-dollar calculated field, map donations by state, add a moving average, and report one insight of their own.

assignments.name: Lab 3: Calculations in Tableau
assignments.description: Using avocado sales data, students build table calculations such as percent of total by market and FIXED and EXCLUDE level of detail expressions, and explain how filters interact with them.

assignments.name: Lab 4: Visualizing spatial data
assignments.description: Did Austin's 2015 Uber ban hurt demand for Airbnb listings that are harder to reach? Students map transit and walk scores, map the change in demand from 2015 to 2016, and cluster listings by location in Tableau.

assignments.name: Data story analysis
assignments.description: Once in the term, a small team opens class with a data story published in the last six months, critiques two or three of its charts with principles from the course, and presents remade versions. Before presenting, teams test the redesign with the AI Data Visualization Coach.

assignments.name: Class participation
assignments.description: Credit in each of the seven modules for in-class quizzes, Tableau workbooks submitted from the lab sessions, or follow-along activities.

items.subject: Netflix content by country and genre
items.approach: Kaggle Netflix titles; Tableau Prep split/pivot of multi-country field, genre grouping; treemap country selector driving line charts
items.description: Compared TV vs. movie output and genre mix across countries; selecting a country (e.g., UK) showed movies dominating over time, with a 2019-2020 dip attributed to the pandemic.

items.subject: Neighborhood income change by zip code
items.approach: Census ACS median income; calculated percent-change fields; filled maps, heat-map coloring, linked table with click-to-filter
items.description: Mapped how median household income shifted by zip code (zooming into Pittsburgh) to raise questions about gentrification and local disparities.

items.subject: Netflix TV vs. movies and kids content
items.approach: Kaggle Netflix titles; genres regrouped; bar, line, stacked bar charts and a geospatial map with an interactive bar chart
items.description: Explored how Netflix's TV/movie mix and children's content shifted over time and where content originates (US, India, UK dominant).

items.subject: YouTube channel revenue drivers
items.approach: YouTube dataset with sparse columns removed; binned metrics, scatter plots with trend lines, text tables, dashboard filters
items.description: Asked which factors drive creator revenue; trend lines and binned views showed which metrics correlate with revenue, with subscribers as the second most important factor.

items.subject: Racial disparities in Nashville traffic stops
items.approach: Stanford Open Policing Project data filtered to 2011-2018; demographic charts, stop-density map, day/hour views, year filter and race highlighting
items.description: Compared stop rates and outcomes (warnings, citations, arrests) by race against Nashville census demographics and tracked declines in stops alongside a 2014 Tennessee bill.

items.subject: MLB payroll vs. wins
items.approach: Baseball Reference wins blended with Spotrac payroll; bar-line combo, scatter with efficiency line, heat map, cost-per-win table; team selector across views
items.description: Showed diminishing returns to payroll, flagging the Yankees as least and the Rays/Pirates as most cost-efficient per win, with COVID-season adjustments.

items.subject: NYC subway ridership recovery after COVID
items.approach: MTA turnstile data; line and area charts, station map sized/colored by ridership and recovery, click/hover filtering
items.description: Compared post- vs. pre-COVID ridership (about 75% recovery headline), rush-hour vs. off-peak shifts, and station-level outliers, linking changes to hybrid work and tourism.

items.subject: U.S. defense procurement spending
items.approach: DoD Green Book, SIPRI, and contract-award data reshaped to long format in constant FY25 dollars; line, stacked area, and bar charts with year/branch/category filters
items.description: Tracked total procurement, branch allocations (including the new Space Force), category growth in software and cyber, and top contractors' market share.

items.subject: Recycling trends for circular products
items.approach: U.S. EPA waste-stream data; time series and bar charts, parameter-driven threshold sliders, year and goods-type filters with some views held unfiltered
items.description: Identified materials (paper, iron-based metals) with enough recycled volume to support circular product development, contrasting declines such as newspapers.

items.subject: Gender gaps in STEM education
items.approach: World Bank indicators on education spending, STEM enrollment, and gender parity (GPI), merged and cleaned; choropleth, line, bar, scatter; calculated field estimating female STEM graduates
items.description: Contrasted girls' academic performance with lower STEM enrollment, mapped education spending, and related government spending to gender parity, ending with policy calls to action.

items.subject: Nurse staffing cost savings in Canadian healthcare
items.approach: Published staffing-shortage and agency-fee figures; parameter inputs for nurses, days, and shifts; side-by-side cost comparison
items.description: A what-if dashboard comparing the cost of filling nursing shifts directly against staffing agencies.

items.subject: Marvel films and comics
items.approach: MCU box office (2008-2019) plus Marvel comics character data, outliers filtered and missing values recoded; split-view dashboard with year-range and hero-gender filters
items.description: Paired MCU revenue/profit trends with new comic character introductions to suggest which emerging heroes could anchor future films.

items.subject: Netflix content production trends
items.approach: Kaggle Netflix titles with multi-value fields split, outliers removed, genres grouped; seasonality, global distribution, release-vs-added charts; date and genre filters
items.description: Examined movies vs. TV, leading countries, genres and directors, COVID effects on additions, and older-title licensing, closing with content-strategy recommendations.

items.subject: Where disabled veterans live
items.approach: VA disability data merged with USDA county statistics and census data; maps, scatterplot with adjustable scale, top/bottom-10 sorted bars, state filter
items.description: Found disproportionate concentrations of disabled veterans in Southern states (e.g., Georgia) relative to total veteran counts and tied this to VA resource allocation.

items.subject: Super Bowl prediction myth-busting
items.approach: NFL regular-season team, quarterback, and Super Bowl stats from multiple sources; scatter plots, treemaps, bubble charts, summary tiles, conference/division filters
items.description: Used offense, defense, and special-teams data to argue the Eagles were underrated relative to near-unanimous media picks for the Chiefs.

items.subject: Supply-chain order analysis for a quotations team
items.approach: Sales and vendor data joined in Tableau; custom bins, treemap, log-scale dual-axis chart, route map, KPI ribbon
items.description: Answered a sales team's questions about order sizes, product lines, and shipping routes.

items.subject: Executive dashboards for a retail superstore
items.approach: Kaggle Superstore data; calculated YoY metrics, forecasting, top/bottom-N lists, filters by year/region/category
items.description: Built separate CEO, CMO, and COO dashboards with role-specific KPIs such as forecasts, discount-profit relationships, and shipping modes.

items.subject: Netflix catalog strategy
items.approach: Kaggle Netflix titles with manual cleaning of multi-country and duration fields; bar charts, trend lines, map; filters by type, rating, country
items.description: Showed rapid catalog growth after 2017, top genres and producing countries, and typical movie runtimes, recommending more family and localized content.

items.subject: Global warming by region and season
items.approach: Kaggle daily city temperatures (1995-2019), incomplete years excluded; slope graphs, time-lapse map, monthly seasonal breakdowns with region/country filters
items.description: Showed which regions and months warmed most, contrasting slightly warmer winters with hotter summers and linking to agriculture (e.g., Florida crops).

items.subject: Netflix international content strategy
items.approach: Kaggle Netflix titles; regional genre and rating views with region/country/genre drill-down
items.description: Framed a content-strategy decision showing mature-rated content dominance in the US vs. other markets and Bollywood's weight in India, recommending more focus on India.

items.subject: Road roughness and traffic accidents
items.approach: National Transportation Atlas Database incl. International Roughness Index; maps plus bar charts with clickable state and road-type filters
items.description: Found road roughness was not the primary accident driver, with 'other road users' the dominant cause, and discussed implications for transportation planning.

items.subject: Netflix global expansion
items.approach: Kaggle Netflix titles with expanded multi-country records and manually curated location data; geospatial map with movie/TV and country comparisons
items.description: Traced Netflix's international expansion, including investment-driven production spikes in India and a TV focus in Japan.

items.subject: Federal student loans and interest rates
items.approach: U.S. Dept. of Education loan data blended with Census population; per-capita normalization, interest-rate averages, state map selector vs. national average
items.description: Showed a negative relationship between interest rates and loan disbursements and framed the dashboard as a forecasting tool for universities' enrollment and budgets.

items.subject: Netflix TV shows vs. movies
items.approach: netflix_titles.csv plus Netflix 2023 engagement report and 10-K data; country comparisons and a correlation analysis
items.description: Argued TV shows are growing globally and correlated TV share with operating income, claiming TV is more efficient per title than movies.

items.subject: Global food trends and restaurants
items.approach: Credited external datasets on food inflation and consumer preferences; trend visuals
items.description: Showed food inflation reducing restaurant share of wallet and younger consumers moving to healthier options, with suggestions for how restaurants adapt.

items.subject: Global terrorism 1990-2020
items.approach: Three decades of attack data; totals, country maps, and attacks by organization
items.description: Showed terrorism spiked then recently dropped, that the Iraq/Afghanistan wars drove much of the count, and that attacks are not confined to one region.

items.subject: Garment factory productivity and incentives
items.approach: Garment factory productivity data (actual vs. targeted, overtime, incentives) by department and team
items.description: Found higher incentives associated with lower productivity for some teams and recommended restructuring the incentive program.

items.subject: Global warming
items.approach: Daily city temperature data (predefined climate project); heat maps, line graphs, box plots
items.description: Compared 1995 and 2019 averages and regional variability to show gradual warming, with some recent regional declines.

items.subject: Spotify revenue and Premium
items.approach: Spotify financials, subscriber and ARPU metrics; revenue/profit trend charts
items.description: Traced revenue and gross profit growth and compared Premium vs. ad revenue around a 2022 change.

items.subject: EV certified vs. actual range in South Korea
items.approach: Public test results from a YouTube channel's standardized route vs. Ministry of Environment certified ranges; ratio by brand and weight class
items.description: Showed actual ranges often exceed certified ones with wide variation by manufacturer and weight class, with suggestions for the regulator.

items.subject: Netflix content strategy
items.approach: Kaggle Netflix titles; library growth and average duration by country of production
items.description: Showed library growth slowing after 2019 amid streaming competition, faster movie than TV growth, and duration patterns across top countries.

items.subject: High-growth careers
items.approach: Occupational employment change and projection data, automation potential, education requirements
items.description: Identified occupations with high projected growth and low automation risk to guide students' career choices.

items.subject: Netflix originals and MPAA ratings
items.approach: Market data on Netflix expansion, original-content investment, Disney+ ad revenue, PG-13 box office share
items.description: Argued that few Netflix originals are rated PG or below and proposed steps on ratings strategy.

items.subject: Formula 1 greats of the decade
items.approach: A decade of F1 results; wins and pole positions by driver and circuit
items.description: Compared Hamilton and Verstappen to name the recent 'G.O.A.T.', with context on regulation changes.

items.subject: NYC restaurant inspections
items.approach: NYC Open Data (Dept. of Health) inspection records, 2021-2023; trend, borough grade distribution, violation trends
items.description: Found steady average scores, more A grades in Manhattan, and a slight rise in bio-hazard violations.

items.subject: Capital vs. labor productivity and GDP
items.approach: World Bank capital stock and real GDP data; comparisons of the U.S., China, and Nigeria
items.description: Asked how capital and labor productivity relate to GDP and attributed sustained U.S. productivity to investment in education and technology.

items.subject: Watch company simulation operations
items.approach: Data from a 12-period MBA capstone business simulation, visualized in Tableau; world map of market share, revenue/ROIC bars, capital structure
items.description: Told the story of the team's simulated company's global market share, financial performance, and capital structure versus competitors.
